cohort: One hundred eight women booked for antenatal care, starting at 24-27 weeks gestation, were divided into an exercise group and a control group.
finding: Women participating in regular antenatal exercises experienced significantly lower rates of maternal request Caesarean Sections, less maternal weight gain, reduced back pain/discomfort, less maternal exhaustion during labour, and a decreased need for episiotomy, with comparable newborn weights.
mod_finding: Mothers in the exercise group had a higher rate of spontaneous vaginal births (46.3% vs 24%) and significantly lower rates of maternal request Caesarean Sections compared to the control group.
